newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels say offensive takes another key town.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say offensive takes another key town.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Monday his forces had captured Kananga, capital of Western Kasai province, and were advancing.

Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), told Reuters by telephone from his headquarters in the eastern town of Goma that his forces "entered and took Kananga on Saturday".
The ADFL now controls about half the country. Kabila said his forces were continuing to advance on Kinshasa but denied giving ailing president, Mobutu Sese Seko, a deadline to quit.

"I never said he should resign in three days. All I said was he had three days to consider making contact with me to discuss his departure," said the guerrilla chief. Kabila said he resumed the offensive after Mobutu declined to consider the offer.
The fall of Kananga, one of the largest towns outside Kinshasa that was still in government hands, was first announced by Kabila's Goma-based Voice of the People radio.

Church sources told Reuters last week that Mobutu's army looted Kananga on April 6 -- a sign throughout the six-month rebellion that the army was about to leave a town. The rebels say they entered six days later.
Rebel radio said the small town of Kasumbalesa on the Zambian border had also fallen as the group consolidated positions in the continent's third largest country.

"Kasumbalesa and Kananga were taken by the Alliance on Friday 11 and Saturday 12 respectively," the radio said. "The fall of Kananga leaves the Alliance in a good position to move on Bandundu whose people are eagerly awaiting liberation." Bandundu is only 270 km (165 miles) northeast of Kinshasa.
Kabila said he would be visiting Zaire's second largest city Lubumbashi "very, very soon". The rebels took Lubumbashi last week, depriving the government of valuable mineral resources.
Kabila's rebels fighting to end Mobutu's 32-year-old hold on power have seized control of the eastern half of the vast country in under six months.

Zaire government troops, former Rwandan government soldiers and extremist Interahamwe militiamen fled 125 km (78 miles) west to Kananga after their defeat at the diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi, which fell to rebels on April 5, witnesses said.
If Kananga has fallen, the rebels are 950 km (593 miles) east of Kinshasa on the southern front. The rebels are using the massive Zaire River to advance through the north of the country.
Voice of the People claimed rebel forces are just 300 km (185 miles) from an increasingly nervous Kinshasa but gave no further details.

Kinshasa was crippled on Monday by a stay-at-home strike called by local opponents of Mobutu, witnesses said. Shops, schools, and businesses were closed and public transport was off the streets as were most private vehicles.

Security forces were out in force in potential flashpoint areas, notably opposition bastions near the Njili airport. The business district was deserted with a few para-military gendarmes manning key intersections.
Supporters of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, who was sacked as prime minister by Mobutu last week after only days in office, are spearheading the anti-Mobutu campaign in the capital.
